In Years 10 and 11, they continue to study core curriculum subjects: English literature and language, maths, statistics, science, Spanish and geography or history alongside their optional choices totaling 10 GCSEs.

The Whitstable School
On Track to Excellence
Welcome to The Whitstable School, a lead school for GCSE and A-Level results in the region. Our pupils cultivate a profound love for learning, consistently striving to reach their full potential. We provide an excellent education that promotes the enjoyment of academic enquiry and fosters creativity, serving as a fundamental building block for every student's progress. At The Whitstable School, we believe your child's happiness is the key to a bright and successful future.
Relationships between staff and pupils are strong, encouraging and supportive. We offer a specialised pathway at key stage 3 for pupils that have a real passion and interest for Performing Arts or STEM (science, technology, engineering & maths). TWS Stage Stage and TWS STEM Academy offer additional lessons, after school enrichment and drop down days.
The best way to discover what life is like at our school is to visit and speak with both staff and pupils.
Alex HolmesHeadteacher

Careers
At The Whitstable School, we understand the importance of careers education for all students in Year 7 through to Year 13. The careers provision we offer seeks to deliver on the Department for Education Careers Statutory Guidance (July 2021). The Whitstable School is working to achieve the 8 Gatsby Careers Benchmarks, which reflect international best practice, to improve careers provision.
In addition to our links with local universities, we are working closely with the Careers and Enterprise Company, who regularly advise us as we work towards the Gatsby Benchmarks which set out best practices for all schools across the country.
Within the school, we have progressed further with careers initiatives by introducing a Careers Hub. This is a fantastic space dedicated to careers which includes software and prospectuses. We have a dedicated, qualified careers' advisor who is able to assist with any questions regarding future prospects.
Careers Team Contact Details:
Email: tws_careers@swale.at Telephone: 01227 931300.
Careers Lead: K Middleton
Careers Advisor: T Rawlinson
Every Friday between 3pm and 4pm, the careers team will be available to speak to students about future plans and aspirations and are able to answer any questions that students might have regarding their next steps.
Parents and carers are welcome to contact our careers team to seek advice and ask any questions they might have regarding career pathways.
Our series of ‘An audience with’ and ‘Spotlight on careers’ ensure we have a variety of guests coming to the school to speak to students about a range of careers and interesting experiences. We also hold a yearly Careers Fair for years 9 – 13 in March.
We welcome enquiries from other providers and guest speakers as outlined in our Policy below. If you would like to come and deliver a talk to students on ‘Spotlight on Careers’ or you would like to be part of our Careers Fair, please contact the team. We are particularly keen to hear from apprenticeship or training providers too.
Below is the whole school Careers Plan which highlights activities taking place over the next school year.

About Us
Student Leadership at The Whitstable School
Student Leadership at The Whitstable School
Empowering the Future: Student Leadership at The Whitstable School
At The Whitstable School, we believe in giving our students a voice and empowering them to be the leaders of tomorrow. Our student leadership programs, particularly within the Sixth Form, provide invaluable opportunities for our young people to make a real difference, develop crucial skills, and inspire their peers.

Highlights of Our Student Leaders' Impact
Exceptional Head Students: We are incredibly proud of our Head Student, Izzy, who has been invited to address Parliament in January, linking her work with the influential Generation FOMO initiative. This remarkable opportunity demonstrates the calibre of our student leaders and their ability to engage with national issues.
Prefects: Our Year 11 Prefects are a vital part of the school community, providing essential support during parents' evenings and spearheading new initiatives across the school. Recently, some of our prefects had the unique opportunity to visit Parliament to learn about the inner workings of government firsthand. For our student leaders aspiring to careers in law and politics, these experiences—coupled with the responsibilities of their role—provide an invaluable asset as they prepare for life beyond school.
Sixth Form Leadership Team: Our dedicated Sixth Form leadership team is at the heart of key initiatives, ensuring student perspectives are heard and acted upon. They work hard to create new leadership opportunities for their peers, demonstrating collaborative effort and strong vision.
Successful Reading Mentorship Scheme: Our leaders champion literacy through the Reading Mentor Scheme. This program, which pairs Sixth Formers with younger students, is a huge success. The positive impact and relationship-building were recently celebrated with a successful Reading Mentor and Mentee trip.
Engaging with Democracy: We, at TWS, think that getting your voice heard is an integral part of school and what better way to do this through being mentor representatives. Pupils meet twice a term to discuss issues that students want to change about the school. The meetings are divided into Year 7 and 8, and Year 9 and 10. Our student leaders don't just talk about change; they see it in action. A group of our student leaders and other students will be taking part in a trip to Parliament, offering them a first-hand look at the democratic process and how they can influence it.
Building Connections: We are always looking for ways to further integrate student voice. We are keen to have our Head Students invited to Pupil Parliaments to build stronger cross-school communication and collaborative action.
Get Involved!
We are committed to expanding our leadership opportunities. Student leaders at The Whitstable School are not just figureheads—they are active agents of positive change within our school and the wider community.

About Us
About Us
The Whitstable School is a vibrant and nurturing community where creativity and academic excellence go hand in hand. Through our specialist academies—STEM and STAGE—and across all subjects, we champion innovation, independence and teamwork. Creativity isn’t just reserved for the arts; it’s embedded in every lesson, from English to mathematics.
Our curriculum is forward-thinking and designed to meet the needs of today’s learners. From Year 8, students can specialise early in a broad range of subjects, including fine art, textiles, dance, and drama—offering pathways rarely available in other schools.
We have a proven track record of high achievement at both GCSE and A Level, with students progressing to top universities, competitive apprenticeships and specialist colleges. Our strong results reflect the dedication of our staff and the ambition of our students.
With a small-school feel, we know every pupil well. Our Ready to Learn and TRACK curriculum provides consistency and pastoral care, with the same tutor supporting each child across five years. This builds strong relationships and a secure foundation for success.
We celebrate our students’ talents and voices at every opportunity and encourage leadership, confidence, and personal growth. As part of the Swale Academies Trust, we benefit from shared expertise, wider resources, and a strong support network to enrich learning even further.
At The Whitstable School, we don’t just educate—we inspire every child to grow, belong, and thrive.

Safeguarding
Operation Encompass
Operation Encompass
The Whitstable School participates in a project that runs jointly between schools and Kent Police.
Operation Encompass is the reporting to schools of any domestic abuse experienced by a child or young person within The Whitstable School.
Operation Encompass will ensure that a member of the school staff known as a Key Adult, is trained to use the information to support the child and family through the possible difficulties experienced.
We are keen to offer the best support possible to all our pupils and we believe this will be extremely beneficial for all those involved.
You can find further information from the Operation Encompass website.
The Key Adults are; Mr Brewster (Lead DSL) and Miss Moore (Safeguarding Officer).
